{{nihongo|'''Inane Shrine'''|稲根神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Mikurajima, Tokyo|Q1354993|qid=Q1354993}}, {{ill|Tokyo|Q1490|qid=Q1490}}. The shrine near the settlement is the haiden; the honden (okumiya) is in Inanegamori, about 4 {{ill|Kilometre|Q828224|qid=Q828224}} to the {{ill|South|Q667|qid=Q667}}. {{nihongo|'''Inane Shrine'''|稲根神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

== History ==
The founding date is unknown. However, since it is identified with the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}} {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} “Itatewake-no-Mikoto Shrine,” it is presumed to have existed at least by the {{ill|Engi (era)|de|Engi (Ära)|fa|انگی (دوره)|fr|Ère Engi|ia|Engi (era)|id|Engi|ja|延喜|ko|엔기|ru|Энги (нэнго)|simple|Engi (era)|sr|Енги (ера)|tr|Engi (dönem)|uk|Енґі (ненґо)|zh|延喜|zh_yue|延喜|qid=Q1374325}} era ({{ill|901|Q23580|qid=Q23580}}-{{ill|923|Q30108|qid=Q30108}}).

According to tradition, long ago people noticed a shining object on Mt. Inane every night, and when they approached they found a {{ill|Mirror|Q35197|qid=Q35197}} hanging on a tree. They then founded a shrine using the mirror as {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}}; this became the origin of the shrine<ref name="神社庁">[http://www.tokyo-jinjacho.or.jp/tosho/7285/ 稲根神社] Tokyo Association of Shinto Shrines</ref>.

The shrine holds works by Taga Chōko (later {{ill|Hanabusa Itchō|de|Hanabusa Itchō|fi|Itchō Hanabusa|fr|Hanabusa Itchō|hy|Հանաբուսա Իտտյո|it|Hanabusa Itchō|ja|英一蝶|ml|ഹനബുസ ഇത്ഛോ|pl|Itchō Hanabusa|ru|Ханабуса Иттё|sv|Hanabusa Itchō|tr|Hanabusa Itchō|uk|Ханабуса Іттьо|zh|英一蝶|qid=Q3109209}}), who was once {{ill|Penal transportation|ar|ترحيل جزائي|ca|Deportació penal|eo|Prizontransportado|es|Destierro penal|fa|تبعید کیفری|fr|Déportation pénale|he|הגליה|id|Hukuman buang|ja|流罪|ko|유배|no|Transportering|ps|جزايي تبعید|pt|Desterro penal|ru|Ссылка (наказание)|tr|Sürgün cezası|zh|流放|zh_yue|流放|qid=Q1770529}} to {{ill|Miyake-jima|ar|مياكي جيما|ast|Miyakejima|az|Miyakecima|ceb|Miyake Jima|cs|Mijakedžima|de|Miyake-jima|eo|Mijakeŝimo|es|Miyakejima|fa|میاکجیما|fr|Miyake-jima|it|Miyakejima|ja|三宅島|ko|미야케섬|lt|Mijakedžima|pnb|میاک-جیما|pt|Ilha Miyake|ru|Мияке (остров)|sk|Mijakedžima|sv|Miyakejima|th|เกาะมิยาเกะ|tl|Miyake, Tokyo|tr|Miyakejima|uk|Міяке (острів)|vi|Miyakejima|zh|三宅島|qid=Q1075076}}: “Panel painting of sacred horse” and “Panel painting of Ōmori Hikoshichi”<ref name="散歩">Tokyo Historical Education Research Society (ed.), ''Historical Walks in Tokyo, Vol.2 (Historical Walk 13): Tama and Islands'', Yamakawa Shuppansha, 2005, p.248</ref>.

Since access to the honden (okumiya) is only via {{ill|Mountain trail|de|Bergweg|es|Sendero de montaña|ja|登山道|sl|Planinska pot|qid=Q913398}}, a guide is required<ref name="観光">[https://tamashima.tokyo/mikurashima/2018/article001-3.html Why Mikurajima is called a miracle island: severe yet beautiful forest-and-sea experience] Tokyo Convention & Visitors Bureau “TAMASHIMA.tokyo”</ref>.

== Cultural properties ==
*Panel painting of sacred horse, by Taga Chōko (Hanabusa Itchō) (Tokyo-designated tangible cultural property, designated Feb 21, Shōwa 32)<ref name="都1">[https://bunkazai.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/jp/search_detail.html?page=1&id=231 板絵着色神馬図額 多賀朝湖（英一蝶）筆] Tokyo</ref>
*Panel painting of Ōmori Hikoshichi, by Taga Chōko (Hanabusa Itchō) (Tokyo-designated tangible cultural property, designated Feb 21, Shōwa 32)<ref name="都2">[https://bunkazai.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/jp/search_detail.html?page=1&id=232 板絵着色大森彦七図額 多賀朝湖（英一蝶）筆] Tokyo</ref>
*Panel painting of islanders’ daily life and labor (Tokyo-designated tangible cultural property, designated Feb 21, Shōwa 32)<ref name="都3">[https://bunkazai.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/jp/search_detail.html?page=1&id=456 板絵着色島民生活労働図額] Tokyo</ref>

== Access ==
*15 minutes on foot from Mikurajima Port (to the haiden).
